description:
PROPOSED, NOT APPLIED. kvim's :term is an interactive surface and CLAUDE.md says to flag rather than auto-fix what cannot be verified without a real terminal. I wrote this patch, could not verify it, and reverted it. Needs the maintainer's dogfooding.

THE BUG, which is unambiguous: crates/kopitiam-neovim/src/termemu.rs build_command() does

    let shell = std::env::var(SHELL).unwrap_or_else(|_| /bin/sh.to_string());
    cmd.arg(-c);

There is no /bin/sh on Windows, and '-c' is not cmd's flag. So ':term ls' on Windows spawns nothing and paints an empty pane with no error. On Termux this is fine (SHELL is set, /bin/sh exists), so it only bites the desktop.

PROPOSED PATCH (cfg-split inside build_command):
  windows  -> %COMSPEC%, else cmd.exe, with /C
  not(windows) -> \, else /bin/sh, with -c
Do NOT consult \ on Windows: Git Bash exports it, and honouring it would hand a cmd-flavoured command line to sh.

WHY I COULD NOT VERIFY IT: the four termemu pty tests still fail on this box after the patch, with an EMPTY screen rather than a spawn error - so TermSession::spawn succeeds and the child produces nothing. That points below the shell choice, at ConPTY itself. Corroborating: kmux's own windows tests fail here with 'ConPTY executable not found on PATH: pwsh.exe' (crates/kmux/src/pty/backend/windows/application.rs:33). Something about ConPTY on this machine is not working, and until that is sorted the pty tests cannot confirm or deny the shell fix.

SECOND, SEPARATE ISSUE FOUND: the pty tests hardcode UNIX COMMANDS - 'printf hello', 'cat', 'exit 3'. Even with a working ConPTY those cannot pass on Windows, because cmd.exe has none of them. If the shell fix lands, they need platform-appropriate commands too: 'echo X' works in both shells, and 'findstr "^"' is the cmd equivalent of 'cat' (matches every line, reprints it). That part is test-only and safe to apply without dogfooding.

ORDER TO DO THIS IN: (1) find out why ConPTY does not work on this box - it blocks both kvim and kmux, and without it nothing here is verifiable; (2) apply the shell fix and confirm ':term ls' actually paints output in a real terminal; (3) make the test commands portable so the suite can hold the line afterwards.
title: kvim: ':term <cmd>' cannot work on Windows - hardcoded /bin/sh -c (patch proposed, needs dogfooding)
